Russia Wheat: Wet Weather Hampers Spring Wheat Sowing
USDA forecasts 2018/19 Russia wheat production at 68.5 million metric tons (mmt), down 3.5
mmt from last month and down 16.5 mmt from last year’s record crop. USDA crop production
estimates for Russia exclude estimated output from Crimea. The forecast yield of 2.74 tons per
hectare is second only to last year’s record. In Russia, winter wheat accounts for about 70
percent of total wheat production and spring wheat accounts for about 30 percent. The estimated
harvested area has been decreased from 26.0 to 25.0 million hectares (mha) based on reports
from the Ministry of Agriculture indicating significant sowing delays in the Siberian District of
Russia, which is the country’s largest producer of spring wheat. Planting is typically complete,
or nearly complete, by the second week of June. This year, however, the Siberian sowing
Approved by the World Agricultural Outlook Board

title: campaign was only about 76 percent complete as of June 6, and final area is unlikely to reach the
text:
campaign was only about 76 percent complete as of June 6, and final area is unlikely to reach the
Ministry forecast of 5.9 mha. If subsequent planting in the Siberian District follows the course
of the 2013 sowing campaign, which was also marked by early delays followed by rapid early-
June planting, wheat area could reach roughly 4.7 mha.
Vegetative indices for the North Caucasus and Southern Districts (Russia’s main winter wheat
production region) show that crop conditions in several important areas were substantially worse
than last year during the second half of May, when the crop was going through the important
flowering stage. This was likely due to below-normal rainfall and above-normal temperatures
during April and May. The winter wheat harvest will begin in late June or early July and
concludes in mid-August. Russia’s spring wheat harvest usually begins in late August and
continues through October.
Area, yield, and production estimates for Russia winter wheat and spring wheat are available on
PSD Online at https://apps.fas.usda.gov/psdonline/app/index.html#/app/downloads, and select
“Downloadable Data Sets.” Select the zipped file for “Russia Wheat: Winter/Spring Area and
Production Breakdown”. (For more information, please contact Mark.Lindeman@fas.usda.gov.)
Germany Wheat: Dryness Lowers Wheat Production
USDA forecasts 2018/19 wheat production in Germany at 23.7 million metric tons (mmt), down
0.8 million or 3 percent from last month and last year, but down 8 percent from the 5-year
average. Area is unchanged from last month at 3.1 million hectares (mha), 4 percent below last
year and last month. Yield is estimated at 7.72 metric tons per hectare (mt/ha), down 3 percent
from last month, down 1 percent from last year, and down 4 percent from the 5-year average.
Dryness during spring
has reduced yield
potential for wheat in
Germany. The dryness
during May was
particularly problematic
because wheat was in the
highly-sensitive
flowering stage when it
is particularly susceptible
to dryness. Excessive
rainfall during planting
last autumn contributed
to the lowest national
area in over 5 years.
Total EU wheat is
estimated at 149.4
million tons, down 1
percent from last year and 2 percent from the 5-year average. Area is unchanged from last month
at 25.8 mha, down 2 percent from last year, and down 3 percent from the 5-year average.

title: Estimated EU harvested area is the lowest in over 10 years. Yield is estimated at 5.79 mt/ha,
text:
Estimated EU harvested area is the lowest in over 10 years. Yield is estimated at 5.79 mt/ha,
down 1 percent from last month, but up 1 percent from the 5-year average. The combination of
the 0.8 million-ton reduction in Germany along with a 0.2 mmt reduction in Poland (dryness
related), totals the 1.0 mmt reduction to the estimated EU crop.
For country-specific area, yield, and production estimates within the European Union (EU),
please go to PSD Online at https://apps.fas.usda.gov/PSDOnline/app/index.html#/app/home, and
select “Downloadable Data Sets.” Select the zipped file for “EU Countries Area & Production.”
(For more information, please contact Bryan.Purcell@fas.usda.gov.)
India: Wheat Production Boosted by Record Yields
USDA estimates 2018/19 wheat production at 97.0 million metric tons, up 2 percent from last
month but down 2 percent from last year. Harvested area is estimated at 30.0 million hectares,
unchanged from last month and down 3 percent from last year because of less than ideal planting
conditions in unirrigated wheat area. Farmers delayed planting and switched to less water
intense crops such as chickpeas and other pulses in Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan because of
the dry and warm conditions during the planting in November. The major wheat areas of Uttar
Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh planted 2 percent and 16 percent less wheat than last year. Year-to-
year harvested area was unchanged in Punjab. However, record yields in irrigated wheat areas
compensated for lower yields and the lower area. Yield is estimated at 3.23 tons per hectare, up 1
percent from the 2017/18 record.
Record yields were reported
in Punjab, Haryana, and
Uttar Pradesh. Average
temperatures were higher
than normal at planting and
then temperatures dropped to
promote vegetative growth
in December and January.
Ideal temperatures and
scattered rainfall were
reported during their
reproductive stages in
February and March.
MODIS Normalized
Difference Vegetation Index
(NDVI) analysis indicated
good vegetation vigor in the northern wheat areas. The crop was able to mature without any
heavy rains, or wind, which could cause damage.
India’s 2018 wheat harvest is complete. Wheat is grown only during the rabi period (October
through April). The majority of this crop is grown under irrigated conditions. The major
producers are Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Haryana, and Bihar. (For more
information, please contact Arnella.Trent@fas.usda.gov).
Foreign Agricultural Service/USDA 3 June 2018
Office of Global Analysis

title: Mexico Wheat: Lowest Production Estimate in 14 years
text:
Mexico Wheat: Lowest Production Estimate in 14 years
USDA estimates Mexico wheat production for 2018/19 at 2.8 million metric tons, down 14
percent from last month and down 20 percent from last year. Harvested area is estimated at
535,000 hectares down 14 percent from last month and down 20 percent from last year. Most
recent official data reports year-to-year declines in planted area for the major states of Sonora
and Baja California of 23 percent and 37 percent, respectively. Yield is estimated at 5.23 metric
tons per hectare unchanged from last month and nearly unchanged from last year.
Wheat production in Mexico is mainly driven by the fall/winter cycle, which accounts for
roughly 98 percent of total production. The top winter wheat producing states are Sonora (45
percent) and Baja California (14 percent). Planting operations for the fall/winter cycle occur in
November and extend through early February, and is heavily dependent on irrigation for crop
development. Harvest for the fall/winter cycle ends in July.
The estimated production is the lowest in the last 14 years reflecting a lower than previously
estimated planted area as farmers opt to plant alternative crops. During the start of the winter
wheat planting campaign, reports of reservoir levels in the major producing regions were
between 20 and 50 percent of their capacity. (For additional information, please contact
Justin.Jenkins@fas.usda.gov)
Brazil Soybeans: 2017/18 Record Yield boosts Production
USDA estimates 2017/18 Brazil soybean production at 119.0 million metric tons (mmt), up 2.0
mmt or 2 percent from last month and up 4 percent from the previous year. Harvested area is
estimated at a record 35.1 million hectares, unchanged from last month but up 4 percent from the
previous year. Yield is estimated at a record 3.39 metric tons per hectare, up 2 percent from last
month and up slightly from the previous year. Favorable weather and improved technology
helped raise yields to record levels almost everywhere, except in the south, which experienced

title: less favorable weather. Harvest is finished in major central and southern soybean producing
text:
less favorable weather. Harvest is finished in major central and southern soybean producing
regions and is almost complete in the north and northeastern regions.
Drought in southern Rio Grande do Sul reduced yields by more than 11 percent from last year;
however, losses in the South were more than offset by the Center-West and Northeast. Yields in
Center-West were above last year by more than 3 percent. The surprise was in the Northeast
where yields exceeded last year’s levels by more than 5 percent, and in Piaui, yields exceeded
last year’s levels by almost 15 percent. Overall, soybean production has been given an extra
boost this year by the exceptionally good rains that occurred in the north and northeastern
regions. In these regions, the Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) from satellite
imagery confirmed very good vegetation health and yields were above-average or at record
levels. (For more information, please contact Maria.Anulacion@fas.usda.gov).
Germany Rapeseed: Dryness at Flowering Lowers Yield
USDA forecasts 2018/19 rapeseed production in Germany at 4.3 million metric tons (mmt),
down 0.5 mmt or 11 percent from last month but nearly unchanged from last year and 18 percent
below the 5-year average. Area is estimated at 1.3 million hectares (mha), unchanged from last
month but down 0.1 mha from last year and 6 percent below the 5-year average. Yield is
estimated at 3.32 metric tons per hectare (mt/ha), down 11 percent from last month, 4 percent
from last year, and 13 percent from the 5-year average.
Foreign Agricultural Service/USDA 5 June 2018
Office of Global Analysis

title: Below-normal spring rainfall has caused problems for rapeseed in Germany, particularly in its
text:
Below-normal spring rainfall has caused problems for rapeseed in Germany, particularly in its
northern rapeseed belt, and to a lesser extent in Poland. The crop was flowering during May (the
period when it is most sensitive to weather extremes), when it was especially warm and dry. The
high temperatures accelerated crop growth, enhanced dryness by lowering soil moisture, and thus
reduced yield potential. Rapeseed is not harvested until July or August and assuming normal
weather it has the ability to produce additional flowers and set pods over several weeks, helping
mitigate negative weather effects. Currently the crop is in early podsaet, so June will be another
critical development month.
Germany is the second largest producer of rapeseed in the European Union (EU) after France
(5.5 million tons estimated for 2018/19), so a reduction in Germany is significant to the EU.
The production change to Germany and a 0.1 million-ton reduction to Poland are the only EU
rapeseed changes for June. Total EU rapeseed production is now forecast at 21.8 mmt, down 3
percent from last month and down 2 percent from last year, and 1 percent from the 5-year
average. Area remains unchanged from last month at 6.8 mha, and nearly unchanged from last
year, but 2 percent above the 5-year average. Yield is estimated at 3.21 mt/ha.
For country-specific area, yield, and production estimates within the European Union (EU),
please go to PSD Online at https://apps.fas.usda.gov/PSDOnline/app/index.html#/app/home, and
select “Downloadable Data Sets.” Select the zipped file for “EU Countries Area & Production.”

title: Argentina Soybeans: Late Rains Further Reduce Yield Prospects for 2017/18
text:
Argentina Soybeans: Late Rains Further Reduce Yield Prospects for 2017/18
Argentina soybean production for 2017/18 is estimated at 37 million metric tons, 5 percent
below last month and 36 percent below last year. Area is estimated at 16.8 million hectares,
down 1 percent from last month and down 8 percent from 2016/17. Yield is estimated at 2.20
tons per hectare, down 4 percent from last month and down 30 percent from last year.
2017/18 was one of the worst seasons for soybeans in Argentina with the majority of the summer
crop experiencing drought conditions. The growing season ended with multiple, heavy rains that
did not benefit yields and delayed harvest. Late rains which came at the end of April and
through May were not helpful to either the early planted soybeans or the later planted soybeans,
which were already too damaged to recuperate. The late rains also caused flooding along
waterways and slowed harvest progress. Harvest is now over 90 percent complete with some
early, heavily saturated fields from the late-season rains finally drying out and allowing harvest
to proceed. (For information, please contact Denise.McWilliams@fas.usda.gov.)
China Rice: Production Estimate Decreased 2% from Last Month
USDA forecasts China’s 2018/19 rice production at 142.2 million metric tons (milled basis),
down approximately 2 percent from last month, 3 percent from last year, and 2 percent from the
5-year average. Area is estimated at 29.5 million hectares, down roughly 2 percent from last
month and down 2 percent from last year. Yield is forecast at 6.89 metric tons per hectare, up
slightly from last month, but down less than 1 percent from last year.

Brazil Corn: 2017/18 Lower Area and Yield for Drought-Affected Second Crop
USDA forecasts 2017/18 Brazil corn production at 85.0 million metric tons (mmt), down 2 mmt
or 2 percent from last month, and down 13.5 mmt or 14 percent from last year. Harvested area is
forecast at 16.9 million hectares (mha), down 0.2 mha or 1 percent from last month and down 4
percent from last year. Compared to the previous year, area planted to second-crop corn is down
5 percent in the principal production regions of the Center-West and South according to Brazil’s
Ministry of Supply (CONAB). Yield is estimated at 5.03 metric tons per hectare, down 1 percent
from last month and down 10 percent from last year due to adverse weather in southern second-
crop corn production areas.
In Paraná (18 percent of second-crop corn production) and Mato Grosso do Sul (14 percent), a
prolonged period of dryness occurred during the critical reproductive stages of the crop, which
reduced soil moisture from the end of March through the beginning of May. Rain returned in
early to mid-May, but was too late to reverse damage to much of the drought-affected crop. In
southern Mato Grosso do Sul and through much of Paraná, the Normalized Difference
Vegetation Index (NDVI) indicates declining crop conditions since mid-April, and minimal
recovery, which is similar to or worse than the drought year of 2016. In Mato Grosso (42
percent of second-crop corn production) and Goiás (12 percent), however, NDVI in corn
production areas indicate late crop development in a few locations but generally good vegetation
conditions, similar to the record year of 2017. The majority of second-crop corn is harvested
from June to September. (For more information, please contact
Maria.Anulacion@fas.usda.gov).
Foreign Agricultural Service/USDA 9 June 2018
Office of Global Analysis

title: China Cotton: Production Estimate Decreased 2% from Last Month
text:
China Cotton: Production Estimate Decreased 2% from Last Month
USDA forecasts China’s 2018/19 cotton production at 26.5 million 480-pound bales (5.77
million metric tons), down 2 percent from last month, 4 percent from last year, and 2 percent
from the 5-year average. Area is estimated at 3.35 million hectares, unchanged from last month
but down 1 percent from last year. Yield is estimated at 1,722 kilograms per hectare (kg/ha)
down 2 percent from month and down 2 percent from last year’s record of 1,761 kg/ha, but up 8
percent from the 5-year average of 1,602 kg/ha. The projected yield is at the long-term trend due
to the continued increasing share of cotton being planted in Xinjiang province where yield has
nearly doubled compared to elsewhere in the country.
Cotton planting is almost complete; it started in April and typically continues through May. The
major production regions are in Xinjiang province as well as in the provinces of Shandong,
Hebei, and Jiangsu. The start of this year’s sowing season has been characterized by favorable
weather and soil moisture across the major cotton regions, facilitating rapid planting and early
crop establishment based on the Standardized Precipitation Index.
Similar to last year, the area is expected to increase the most in Xinjiang, and decrease in the
provinces of Shandong, Hebei, and Jiangsu. According to the National Cotton Monitoring
Network, Xinjiang province planted over 2 million hectares last year, increasing its cotton
production to roughly 78 percent of the national total. For five seasons prior to 2017, area
declined due to changes in agricultural policy, specifically the central government’s enactment of

Cote d’Ivoire Cotton: 2017/18 Output Above Average
Cote d’Ivoire’s cotton production for 2017/18 is estimated at 785,000 480-pound bales, up 26
percent from the 2016/17 marketing year and up 8 percent from the 5-year average. Harvested
area is estimated at 0.37 million hectares, up 21,000 hectares or 6 percent from the previous year.
Yield is estimated at 467 kilograms per hectare (kg/ha), up 11 percent from the 5-year average
yield of 421 kg/ha. Seasonal rainfall for 2017/18 crop was favorable throughout the season, with
an estimated two-thirds of the crop considered first-quality. Good quality cotton was harvested
this year due to favorable weather and increased investment during the past several years. The
cotton sector is experiencing a revival from renewed interest and investment, after experiencing
nearly a decade of neglect due to the political crisis caused by a civil war that started in late
2002.
Approximately 95 percent of Cote d’Ivoire’s cotton is grown in the northern Savanes
District and in the central Woroba and Sassandra-Marahoue Districts. Cotton ginning is
also concentrated in these northern and central districts. Ginning mills typically collect
and process the harvest through March. Cote d’Ivoire’s cotton is sown from late May to
early July and harvest generally begins in October and continues through December. (For
more information, please contact Curt.Reynolds@fas.usda.gov.)
